A 1998-ban alakult Baltazár Színház az egyetlen olyan színtársulat Magyarországon, melynek tagjai értelmi sérült színészek. „A Baltazár egyszerre lát el művészi és társadalmi feladatot, hiszen lehetőséget teremt sérült emberek számára, hogy tehetségüket megmutassák, a nézők számára pedig, hogy szembesüljenek e tehetséggel. A színház legfontosabb célkitűzése, hogy magas színvonalon hozzon létre előadásokat, és ezáltal bebizonyítsa, a sérült emberekkel kapcsolatos előítéletek átírhatók: e társadalmi csoport erejét mutatja meg, és azt, hogyan lesz általuk színesebb és gazdagabb a világ” – olvasható a társulat honlapján . Laudációjában Lénárt Gábor, a Színházi Kritikusok Céhének elnökségi tagja kiemelte: Elek Dóra a Baltazár Színház 1998-as megalapításával nem terápiás csoportot, szabadidős foglalkozást vagy jótékonysági kezdeményezést indított útjára, hanem színházat alapított, amelyben a fogyatékossággal élő résztvevők alkotóművészként lépnek színpadra. „A Baltazár társulatában 28 éve folyik a következetes munka, amely – mint minden jó színház – a résztvevő alkotók számára új önfelfedezést kínál. Az előadásokban fogyatékossággal élő és nem fogyatékossággal élő színészek, zenészek, művészek dolgoznak együtt.” A Színházi Kritikusok Céhe 2022-ben alapította meg a Jövő díjat, és azzal az első alkalommal két színházi nevelési társulatot, a Káva Színházat és a Kerekasztal Színházat ismert el, 2023-ban a Soltis Lajos Színházat, 2024-ben a Stereo Aktot tüntetett ki, majd 2025-ben az Apertúra kapta meg az elismerést. Beállítom The Tisza Party’s parliamentary group has nominated András Baka, the former head of the country's Supreme Court as president of Hungary, the party has announced following their Saturday meeting where the decision was made by secret ballot. Although the previous president, Tamás Sulyok’s mandate was supposed to last until March 2029, his term was ended prematurely by the 17th amendment to the Fundamental Law in mid-July. The move was part of the Tisza Party’s campaign promise to remove all “puppets appointed by Fidesz to do their bidding”. In his post announcing Baka’s nomination, Prime Minister Péter Magyar wrote: “Throughout his entire career, Dr. András Baka has regarded the principle of the separation of powers of paramount importance and has always consistently stood up for the rule of law and judicial independence. His life’s work exemplifies a commitment to the democratic rule of law and constitutional principles.” Magyar added that they are convinced that Baka’s “experience and the professional independence he has demonstrated throughout his career are of particular value during this time, as we work together to lay the foundations for Hungary’s new constitutional order.” According to the Prime Minister, during the constitutional process ahead of us, we need a president whose “professional authority, independence, and experience in public law and constitutional matters provide a solid foundation for successfully guiding our country back onto the path of the rule of law and constitutional governance, and for embodying the unity of the Hungarian nation.” —and they consider Baka worthy of the task. András Baka is a researcher specializing in human rights and minority rights issues. He became particularly well-known in 2011 when he was unlawfully removed from his position as president of the Supreme Court after criticizing the Orbán regime’s plans for reforming the judiciary. He was born in Budapest in 1952 and earned his doctorate in law from the Faculty of Law and Political Science at Budapest’s ELTE (Eötvös Lóránd University) in 1978, then worked for more than twenty years as a research fellow at the Institute of Political and Legal Sciences of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences (MTA), and later served as director general of the College of Public Administration. Between 1991 and 2008, he spent two terms serving as a judge at the European Court of Human Rights. ​​Starting in the 1980s, he was a visiting professor at several universities in the United States and has been invited on multiple occasions to lecture in France and (what was then) West Germany. During the first parliamentary term following the regime change in Hungary, between 1990-1991, Baka served as a member of Parliament for the Hungarian Democratic Forum (MDF), though he never joined the party. He also has a background in labor unions. In June 2016, the Grand Chamber at the European Court of Human Rights ruled in Baka's favor and found that he had been removed from his position as head of the Supreme Court in 2012 through ad hominem legislation due to his criticism of the Orbán government's planned judicial reforms, which threatened the independence of the courts. Subsequently, the Council of Europe’s Committee of Ministers held the Hungarian state accountable for failing to implement the Strasbourg judgment in the case of Baka v. Hungary since 2016. He is likely to take office on 19 August Parliament could elect the new head of state as early as Tuesday. The vote is expected to be a mere formality, as the election of the new head of state requires the support of two-thirds of the members of Parliament, and the 141-member Tisza faction has a comfortable majority. The new president shall take office on the eighth day following the announcement of the results of Tuesday’s secret ballot, which would in this case be 19 August. In this case, the new president would be the one to present the state honors and awards customarily announced on August 20, the national holiday celebrating the founding of the Hungarian state. Pursuant to Amendment 17 of the Fundamental Law, the term of the new head of state will last until the new constitution enters into force, but no longer than five years. Previously, Péter Magyar has said that the next President of Hungary must be someone who will watch over the nation’s unity and the rule of law. According to him, the country needs someone who understands the weight of their words, is capable of calm deliberation, is willing to listen to different opinions, and is aware that all decisions they make have consequences. The former governing party, Fidesz and their coalition partner, the Christian Democratic People's party (KDNP) will not participate in electing the new head of state. They had previously indicated that they would boycott the vote because they considered Tamás Sulyok’s removal to be illegitimate. “It’s a wasted effort. Under public law, this is invalid, so holding a presidential election is pointless. The position is not vacant,” they stated . Mi Hazánk nominated energy lawyer Máté Tóth for the position, which, without the support of other parliamentary groups, can essentially be considered only a symbolic gesture, since they only have six representatives in Parliament, and the endorsement of at least one-fifth of the representatives—that is, 40 members—is required for a candidate’s name to appear on the ballot. There were ten candidates In his post on Saturday, Péter Magyar wrote that thousands of Hungarians have recommended dozens of candidates to the Tisza Party in recent weeks, including numerous distinguished experts and well-known public figures. The Tisza Party's leadership interviewed ten candidates, eventually recommending three of them to the Tisza Party's parliamentary faction on Saturday. “We are proud that, for the first time since the transition to democracy, the selection of the head of state did not involve a decision based on deals between parties or choosing from among candidates nominated by parties. Instead, the person we are recommending to lead the nation is a truly independent, nonpartisan individual with a proven track record throughout his life and profession”, the Prime Minister stated. https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026.text: A woman’s body was found in Stanley Park in the Anfield area of Liverpool. Photograph: Paul Ellis/AFP/Getty Images View image in fullscreen A woman’s body was found in Stanley Park in the Anfield area of Liverpool. Photograph: Paul Ellis/AFP/Getty Images Liverpool Police appeal after unidentified woman’s body found in Liverpool park Body of victim thought to be in her 70s found in bin bag in walled garden area of Stanley Park on Friday Hannah Al-Othman North of England correspondent Mon 31 Aug 2026 13.58 EDT Last modified on Mon 31 Aug 2026 14.00 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Police in Liverpool have urged members of the public to come forward with information after the body of an unknown woman believed to be in her 70s was found in a black bin bag in a popular park. Merseyside police were contacted by a passerby who had found the woman’s body in Stanley Park, in the Anfield area of Liverpool, at about 5.25pm on Friday 28 August. The body was found in a black bin bag in the walled garden area of the park. It is believed that it may have lain there undiscovered for a number of weeks. “A postmortem took place on Saturday 29 August, the result of which has been withheld for investigation reasons,” Det Supt Rachel Wilson said at a press conference on Monday. “Our team have since been carrying out extensive enquiries to identify the woman, but we have so far been unable to do so.” Wilson said forensic work continued, adding: “We’re carrying out house-to-house, CCTV and other enquiries as a matter of urgency, but of course the methodical nature of such work can mean it takes time.” Officers believe the woman was in her 70s. She was described as white, about 1.57 metres (5ft 2in) tall, of small build, and with strawberry-blond hair. She was found wearing a pink Nike T-shirt. “Missing people reports in Merseyside and elsewhere have been checked but, so far, these have not resulted in an identification,” Wilson said. “Sometimes people go missing without those close to them realising, through holidays being planned or simple misunderstandings, and so we may not have received a report of any concerns. “While we do not want to worry people unnecessarily, it is vital that we follow every possible lead, both to rule people out and ultimately to identify the woman, notify her next of kin and apprehend the offender.” Describing the murder as a “shocking crime”, Wilson said police were “doing all we can to identify the person or persons responsible and bring them to justice”. Stanley Park separates the Anfield and Goodison Park football stadiums, which are respectively home to Liverpool FC and Everton Women. Assistant chief constable Andy Ryan said he understood “how unnerving” the discovery and the heightened police presence would be for local people, adding: “This is the exact reason that we are so determined to get answers as soon as we possibly can.” He described the park as “a very busy and popular green space, especially in the recent warm summer weeks”. “It is visited by dog walkers and families, as well as people walking and exercising,” he said. “It is quite possible that one or more of these visitors may have seen something suspicious recently and not reported it at the time.” “I want to reiterate Rachel’s appeal,” Ryan added. “If anyone recognises the description of this woman or you have any concerns whatsoever about someone you may know and haven’t seen or heard from recently, please tell us as a matter of urgency.” Potential witnesses are urged to contact Merseyside police via social media or to call 101, quoting reference number 26000706383. Reports can also be made anonymously by calling Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111. Speaking during the high-level general debate of the 81st United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York, Zelensky said Russia managed to capture just over 1,000 square kilometers (roughly 386 square miles) of Ukrainian territory. JOIN US ON TELEGRAM Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official . “And we have already liberated a significant part of it,” he continued. According to him, Russian President Vladimir Putin had spent about 284 people per kilometer (approximately 736 people per square mile). Zelensky calls Putin ‘patient zero’ During his UN address, Zelensky repeatedly referred to Putin as “patient zero” – the man from whom the war began to spread. Advertisement “The more freedom Putin has to act, the more dangerous the word becomes for everyone else,” he said according to a live broadcast from Clash Reports. According to him, Putin reiterated to senior US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner – who visited both Moscow and Kyiv early September in an effort to broker an end to the war – that Russia would seize the Donetsk region within a few months. As of July, the Kremlin is seeking to seize all of the Donetsk region while retaining occupied parts of Sumy and Kharkiv regions as permanent buffer zones. That position would mean Moscow is no longer considering returning occupied land in the northeast in exchange for Ukraine ceding the remainder of Donetsk and Luhansk regions. Other Topics of Interest Lavrov Tells UN Security Council Russia Won’t Pause the War During Negotiations Ukraine’s FM Andrii Sybiha called for Russia’s removal from the Security Council and urged members to demand humanitarian corridors for occupied Oleshky. However, Ukraine categorically rejects giving up any of its territory as a precondition for a settlement. “This is probably the 17th or 18th time in five years that he has made this promise,” Zelensky said . During this year alone, Russia has used more than 2,100 missiles against Ukraine, including more than 950 ballistic missiles, along with 63,000 attack drones. Sikorski: Russia ‘cannot win’ While Zelensky accused Moscow of abusing its UN veto and threatening Moldova, Poland and the Baltic states, Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski framed the escalation as panic. Advertisement “You have been trying to conquer Donbas for over 12 years, and Kyiv for over four,” Sikorski said , adding that Russia is running out of resources to sustain its war effort. “You have been stopped by heroic Ukraine, a country with one tenth of Russia’s gross domestic product (GDP),” he continued , noting that Poland’s economy is almost half the size of Russia’s, while Europe’s is 10 times larger and NATO’s is 25 times larger. “You cannot win,” Sikorski concluded. His remarks echo repeated warnings from Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk, who previously said Russia was preparing “very seriously for an escalation of tension” in the region, with autumn and winter remaining key. On Sept. 18, he also warned that intelligence assessments point to Russian plans for “hybrid” drone and missile strikes on Ukraine’s Western allies , including Poland. Speaking during the Atlantic Council’s virtual event, “Did Russia intentionally target Western officials?” on Tuesday, former CIA Director David Petraeus said Western officials assess that Russia is losing about 6,000 more personnel each month than it recruits. Advertisement The event centered on the Sept. 13 Russian drone strike at the Yahodyn station near the Polish border , where a passenger-train locomotive was hit shortly after a diplomatic train carrying Boris Johnson and other Western officials passed through. Petraeus was on another train nearby. Zelensky’s general warning to Russia ahead of winter The winter, which Zelensky said had fought on Russia’s side for centuries, could now work against Moscow as Ukraine is prepared to reciprocate Russia’s strikes on critical infrastructure. “This winter could be very harsh for us, but in response, we will have no choice but to make it painful for Russia too,” he said . Additionally, Zelensky urged the representatives of 47 countries – including Ghana, Nepal, Tajikistan, India, Yemen, Kenya, Zimbabwe, Cuba, Belarus, Sudan and South Africa – to protect their citizens from Russia’s war. “They’re your citizens. Take care of them and do not let them end up on another front,” Zelensky said. “Do not let Putin drag you into this war.” Earlier this month, Amnesty International Secretary General Agnès Callamard said Russia lures foreign nationals into the war with false job offers, coercion and confiscated passports , which amounts to human trafficking, as defined under the UN’s Palermo Protocol. Advertisement Over the past several months, Ukraine has been intensively preparing for its fifth winter of Russia’s aggression. Kyiv is readying its critical sectors amid widespread expectations that Russia will again target the power grid, heating, and water supplies. Meanwhile, Ukraine continues to appeal to partners for Patriots it urgently needs to intercept Russian ballistic missiles. On Sept. 8, Ukraine signed contracts for about 1,000 Patriot missiles , financed through an EU loan. Separately on the same day, Germany pledged to send PAC-2 interceptors from its existing Bundeswehr (Germany military) stocks. US President Donald Trump reiterated his previous decision to grant Ukraine the license to produce Patriot interceptors domestically on Tuesday, though no formal agreement was reached.
